The *Suppabuddhakuṭṭhi Sutta* (Ud 5.3, PTS Ud 48) is a discourse in the *Udāna* collection of the Pali Canon. The narrative centers on Suppabuddha, a man afflicted with leprosy, who listens to the Buddha's teaching, attains stream-entry, and upon his death is reborn as a deva. The sutta is also referenced in later exegetical literature, specifically the *Desanāhāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4).

Curated passage-level parallels for its verses are found in various recensions of the *Udānavarga*, including the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 28, Pāpavarga), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 28), and Chinese translations such as T 212.29 and T 213.28.
